entry.title: Nobel Prize for IceCube
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Royal Swedish Academy of Science announced on 6 October that the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics goes to Francis Halzen, IceCube principal investigator, for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. Wisconsin Public Radio has since interviewed him about the prize and the importance of neutrino research. The KM3NeT Collaboration sent its congratulations, and the whole South Pole station gathered at the IceCube Lab for a celebratory photograph.

entry.title: ESFRI Landmark status
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The KM3NeT Collaboration announced on 16 October that it has been recognised as a Landmark in the ESFRI Roadmap 2026. ESFRI is the European Strategy Forum on Research Infrastructures, and its Roadmap is updated periodically to identify the most critical next-generation scientific facilities.

entry.title: ARCA and ORCA construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. KM3NeT reported a period of intense marine operations, with two further steps completed for ARCA and ORCA in the week before 9 October. For ARCA, Cable Termination Frame 3 was installed at the deep-sea site during a campaign conducted by Alcatel Submarine Networks.

entry.title: Baikal-GVD point sources
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Baikal-GVD is a cubic-kilometre-scale detector under construction in Lake Baikal, now 70% complete and taking data in partial configurations since 2016. A search for point-like astrophysical sources in a five-year track-like dataset from 2019-2024 found no significant source, so upper limits were computed for a selection of candidates. These are compared with published results from IceCube, ANTARES and KM3NeT.

entry.title: IceCube infrared flares
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A new IceCube paper searches for high-energy neutrinos from infrared flares. It is motivated by neutrino emission already seen from the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068, which points to accretion onto supermassive black holes as a candidate origin of the diffuse flux. The record gives no result for the search.

entry.title: T2K near-detector upgrade
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The leading systematic uncertainties in T2K's oscillation analysis come from modelling neutrino-nucleus interactions, and are largely constrained by measurements at the ND280 near detector. The ND280 upgrade was completed in 2024. One new paper presents a selection of muon-neutrino charged-current events with single positively charged pion production in the new modules, and another proposes a neural network to identify particles in the SuperFGD.

entry.title: Gallium anomaly and the Sun
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A preprint reconsiders the Gallium Anomaly by using the Sun as a neutrino source calibrated through neutrino-electron elastic scattering in terrestrial detectors. It finds the measured gallium capture rate of 66.1±3.1 SNU from SAGE and Gallex/GNO in good agreement with the total measured solar source strength of 67.5 (+1.4, -1.1) SNU, and concludes the result is not anomalous.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper examines the contribution of Δ-direct-Urca processes to neutrino emissivity in neutron stars that may contain Δ isobars. These processes add to the nucleonic and hyperonic Urca channels that are regarded as dominant cooling mechanisms, so the result bears on neutron-star thermal evolution.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors compute two-neutrino double-beta decay rates without decoupling nuclear structure from the lepton kinematics, and compare with the closure, non-closure and Taylor-expansion approximations for 82Se and 136Xe. Anyone using these rates or the electron spectra in double-beta searches should note that deviations from the traditional methods are reported.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies a gauged U(1) Lμ-Lτ model with an ultralight vector boson that kinetically mixes with the photon and so adds a matter potential in the Sun, modifying MSW oscillations. It uses solar measurements from Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande, and discusses prospects for JUNO and XLZD.

entry.title: The authors ask whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be detected through nuclea
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors ask whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be detected through nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals. They include variations in neutron-star mass, failed supernovae that form black holes, and the nuclear equation of state, and quantify how sensitivity grows for models with larger neutrino emission.

entry.title: The paper examines how scalar-mediated neutrino self-interactions, acting during propagation through the cosmi
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper examines how scalar-mediated neutrino self-interactions, acting during propagation through the cosmic neutrino background, would leave spectral imprints on the diffuse supernova neutrino background. It uses a full three-flavour framework with the complete PMNS structure, which matters for next-generation detectors expected to observe this flux.

entry.title: The authors study neutrino mass and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, where masses a
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors study neutrino mass and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, where masses arise from a dimension-7 operator at tree level and a dimension-5 operator at one loop. The model accommodates sub-eV neutrino masses with new physics at the TeV scale, and the paper tests whether thermal leptogenesis is viable there, which differs from canonical seesaw leptogenesis.
